**August 24, 1931 — a Monday**

You were born at what may have been the single worst moment of the twentieth century's worst economic catastrophe — into a world that did not yet know how much worse things were about to get.

**The exact day — Britain's government falls:** On August 24, 1931, the Labour government of Ramsay MacDonald collapsed. The cabinet had been unable to agree on cuts to unemployment benefits demanded by bankers as the price of an emergency loan to stabilize the pound. MacDonald, facing the ruin of his party's core commitments, went to the King and resigned — then, to the shock and fury of nearly everyone in Labour, immediately accepted an invitation to form a cross-party National Government to manage the crisis. He was denounced as a traitor by his own movement. The National Government he assembled that day would govern Britain through the Depression, the abdication crisis, the appeasement years, and into the Second World War. British politics were upended on the day you arrived.

**The world you were born into — the Depression at its nadir:** 1931 is arguably the worst year of the Great Depression. American unemployment was approaching 20 percent. Banks were failing across Europe in cascading waves — the Austrian Creditanstalt had collapsed in May, triggering a European banking crisis that spread through the summer. Germany's financial system was buckling under reparations, debt, and mass unemployment that was feeding the extremist parties on both ends of the political spectrum. The global trading system was seizing. Governments that had promised prosperity were losing their legitimacy faster than they could explain what had gone wrong.

**Fifty-five days after your birth — Thomas Edison dies:** On October 18, 1931, Thomas Edison died at 84. He had been alive for your entire life to that point — a man whose inventions included the phonograph, the motion picture camera, and practical electric light. The world you were born into was still largely running on his infrastructure. You have lived from Edison's death to the James Webb Space Telescope transmitting images from the edge of the observable universe.

**Twenty-five days after your birth — the path to World War II opens:** On September 18, 1931, Japanese officers in Manchuria staged a false-flag explosion on a railway and used it as a pretext to invade. The League of Nations, the institution the world had built after WWI to prevent exactly this kind of aggression, proved unable to stop it. The lesson ambitious militaries drew from Manchuria — that the international order would not enforce itself — echoed through the decade that followed. You were one month old when the system meant to prevent another world war demonstrated it could not.

**The catastrophe that defined your childhood:** Hitler became Chancellor of Germany when you were 18 months old. You were 8 when Germany invaded Poland and the Second World War began. You were 10 when Japan bombed Pearl Harbor and the United States entered the war. You were 13 and 14 years old for the war's final convulsions — the liberation of the death camps, the firebombing of Dresden and Tokyo, the atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Most people learn about these events from books. You were a child present in the world while they happened.

**What your 95 years span:** You were born 28 years after the Wright Brothers' first flight at Kitty Hawk and have lived to see spacecraft land on Mars. You were born when Herbert Hoover was president — a man whose name became synonymous with failure — and have now outlived every president through the current one. You were alive before television, before antibiotics were widely available, before the polio vaccine, before jet travel, before computers, before the internet, before smartphones. You have watched the global population grow from roughly 2 billion to more than 8 billion.

**The compressed improbability of a 95-year life:** At your birth, life expectancy at birth in the United States was roughly 59 years. You have outlived the statistical expectation of your birth year by more than three and a half decades. You have outlived World War II, the Korean War, Vietnam, the Cold War, the Soviet Union, and every world leader who was in power when you were born. You were born into the worst year of the worst economic crisis in modern history, in a world that was 18 months away from Hitler's rise and 8 years from global war — and you are still here.

The Monday you arrived, Britain's government was collapsing and the Depression was tightening its grip on every continent. No one holding you that day could have imagined the world of 2026, or believed that the infant in their arms would live to see it.
